title: A Yeouido Day
fitReason: Seoul's financial island has world-class malls, the Han River, and a skyline you won't forget.

stops.name: Yeouido Han River Park
stops.description: Start with a riverside walk along the Han. Rent a bike and cruise along the water while the city wakes up.
stops.tip: Bikesharing kiosks are right at the park entrance. ₩1,000/hour for the orange Ddareungi bikes.

stops.name: The Hyundai Seoul
stops.description: Korea's most beautifully designed mall — a 3-story indoor forest under a glass ceiling, K-fashion pop-ups, luxury brands, and the best indoor architecture in the city.
stops.tip: 5th floor has quieter cafés with skyline views. Blue Bottle Coffee inside the mall is a solid stop. The weekend GOTCHA GOTCHA vending machine on B2 has a line for a reason.

stops.name: The Hyundai B2 Food Hall
stops.description: 50+ food vendors in one basement — Korean, Japanese, Italian, and desserts that'll make you forget everything else.
stops.tip: Far right wing is less crowded. The wagyu sandwich spot near the escalator is legendary.

stops.name: IFC Seoul Mall
stops.description: Sleek underground mall in the finance district with international brands, a good food court, and direct subway access.
stops.tip: The basement floor has a great Mega Coffee and a bakery. Cooler and less crowded than Hyundai.

stops.name: 63 Building Sky Art
stops.description: Seoul's golden skyscraper with an observation deck and wax museum. The Han River and city panorama at golden hour is stunning.
stops.tip: Combo ticket (wax museum + observation) is best value. Go right before sunset.

stops.name: Han River Night Picnic
stops.description: Grab fried chicken and cold cider from the GS25 riverside store, spread out on a rental mat, and watch Seoul's lights reflect on the water.
stops.tip: Mat rentals ₩3,000. The spot between the two bridges has the best unobstructed skyline view.

title: Old Seoul, All Day
fitReason: The soul of Korea in one neighborhood — five centuries of history within walking distance.

stops.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
stops.description: Korea's grandest palace — more impressive in person than any photo suggests. Guard-changing ceremony runs at 10 AM and 2 PM.
stops.tip: Rent hanbok at the gate (₩15,000) for free entry + amazing photos in the courtyard. Get there early.

stops.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
stops.description: 600-year-old alleyways of traditional Korean homes. The view from Alley 11 — hanok rooftops with modern Seoul behind — is the most photographed shot in the city.
stops.tip: Quiet before 11 AM. Be respectful — real families live here. No loud talking in the residential alleys.

stops.name: Tongin Market Dosirak Café
stops.description: Buy tokens at the entrance, then fill a lunchbox from 30 stalls of traditional Korean dishes. One of the most unique food experiences in Seoul.
stops.tip: ₩5,000 gets you 5 tokens. Try the tteok (rice cake), hotteok (sweet pancake), and ojingeo-twigim (fried squid).

stops.name: Insadong
stops.description: Antique shops, traditional craft galleries, and the Ssamziegil courtyard. Best street in Seoul for unique, handmade gifts and Korean art.
stops.tip: Ssamziegil has the most interesting vendors — spiral courtyard with 70+ small shops. Skip the tourist trinkets near the entrance.

stops.name: Cha Masineun Ttul (Traditional Tea House)
stops.description: Seoul's most beautiful tea house — set inside a 100-year-old hanok. Order the omija (five-flavored berry) tea and slow down completely.
stops.tip: Sit in the inner courtyard if available. Cash preferred. The walnut cookies are homemade.

stops.name: Euljiro Nogaridari (Beer Alley)
stops.description: The most iconic nighttime experience in old Seoul — outdoor tables under Daelim Arcade, cold draft beer, and dried fish snacks (nogari) that go for ₩5,000 a plate. Pure local energy.
stops.tip: Mansen Hopeu is the anchor stall but any outdoor table will do. Order the maneul tongdak (whole fried chicken) to share. This is where Seoulites actually come after work.

title: The Cool Seoul Crawl
fitReason: Seoul's most creative neighborhood — converted factories, indie brands, and a coffee scene that rivals Tokyo.

stops.name: Fritz Coffee Seongsu
stops.description: Seoul's most cult-loved specialty roaster in a converted factory. The croissants sell out fast — the coffee is worth any wait.
stops.tip: Arrive right when they open. Order a flat white and the morning bun. The back room has more seating.

stops.name: Cafe Onion Seongsu
stops.description: A 1970s factory transformed into Seoul's most-photographed café. Industrial concrete walls, exposed steel, and pastries that justify the queue.
stops.tip: The rooftop terrace is hidden up the back stairs. Worth the extra 2 minutes to find it.

stops.name: Seongsu Pop-up Street
stops.description: Korea's most dynamic retail district — new pop-ups open every week from Korean fashion brands, artists, and food concepts you can't find anywhere else.
stops.tip: Check @seongsu.official the night before for what's open. Bring cash. Most pop-ups are small and crowded.

stops.name: Seoul Forest
stops.description: A vast urban forest with a deer garden, butterfly greenhouse, and riverside trails. The deer will eat from your hand in the morning.
stops.tip: Deer feeding is in the morning only. The ecological garden (second section) is less crowded and more beautiful.

stops.name: Seongsu-dong Dinner
stops.description: The back streets of Seongsu have some of Seoul's best restaurants — Korean BBQ, handmade pasta, Japanese izakaya, all in repurposed factory spaces.
stops.tip: Naver Map search 성수동 맛집 and sort by newest reviews. The area around Concave Café has the best density.

title: Gangnam Proper
fitReason: K-beauty flagships, Seoul's best temples, and a tree-lined boulevard that proves Gangnam is more than the song.

stops.name: Bongeunsa Temple
stops.description: A 1,200-year-old Buddhist temple standing quietly between Gangnam's towers. The giant Mireuk Buddha statue and the morning drum ceremony are genuinely moving.
stops.tip: Morning ceremony starts at 4 AM for early risers; normal visiting hours 9 AM–6 PM. Free to enter. The lotus lanterns (spring) are magical.

stops.name: COEX Starfield Library
stops.description: A 13-meter wall of books under a glass ceiling — one of Seoul's most iconic interiors. Free to browse, completely open, and stunning for photos.
stops.tip: Golden hour light (5–6 PM) is best for photos. The reading chairs are legitimately comfortable — bring a book.

stops.name: Gangnam Gyoja
stops.description: Michelin-recognized hand-cut noodles and dumplings just off Gangnam Station. The rich chicken broth kalguksu is one of the best bowls in Seoul for the price.
stops.tip: Get the kalguksu and an order of mandu. Weekday lunch hours (12–1 PM) have shorter waits than weekends.

stops.name: Garosu-gil
stops.description: Seoul's most charming boulevard — ginkgo trees, boutique concept stores, international restaurants, and cafés with the best window seats in the city.
stops.tip: Start from the north end near Sinsa station and walk south. The side alleys are better than the main street.

stops.name: Olive Young Gangnam Town
stops.description: Korea's biggest K-beauty destination — 5 floors of skincare, makeup, and wellness from 200+ Korean brands. Staff give free consultations.
stops.tip: Bring a shopping list — it's overwhelming in a good way. The basement floor has indie Korean brands not available elsewhere.

stops.name: Gangnam Dinner
stops.description: Garosu-gil and the surrounding streets have some of Seoul's best restaurants. Korean BBQ, pasta, tasting menus — all within a 5-minute walk.
stops.tip: Reservations recommended on weekends. Naver Map 가로수길 맛집 and filter by highest rated.

title: The Hongdae Loop
fitReason: Youth culture, street performances, the best café scene in Seoul, and nightlife that runs till sunrise.

stops.name: Anthracite Coffee Hongdae
stops.description: Seoul's most famous specialty café in a former shoe factory. High ceilings, rough concrete, and espresso that coffee nerds fly to Seoul for.
stops.tip: Sit at the bar facing the roasters if you want to talk coffee. The cold brew concentrate is a good takeaway.

stops.name: Hongdae Free Performance Zone
stops.description: K-pop dance crews battle it out every weekend at this outdoor stage. No schedule, no tickets — just show up. One of the most electric free shows in Asia.
stops.tip: Weekends only, noon–4 PM is peak. The area near Exit 9 is the main performance hub. Check in from multiple angles.

stops.name: Tuk Tuk Noodle Thai
stops.description: Michelin Bib Gourmand Thai restaurant in Yeonnam-dong — the most authentic tom yum and pad thai in Seoul. The kind of place Michelin inspectors eat at, not just tourists.
stops.tip: Order the khao man gai (Thai chicken rice) and the green curry. Line forms outside; go at 1:30 PM to catch a slight lull between the main rushes.

stops.name: Ewha University Street
stops.description: Affordable Korean fashion, accessories, and beauty products on the shopping street near Ewha Womans University. Good prices, eclectic styles.
stops.tip: The underground shopping arcade (지하쇼핑) has the best deals. Korean hair accessories and beauty tools are especially cheap here.

stops.name: Hongdae Main Street
stops.description: Indie boutiques, streetwear, vintage stores, and K-beauty shops all within a few hundred meters. The density of interesting shops per block is unmatched.
stops.tip: The alley running parallel to the main street (one block east) has more local, less touristy shops.

stops.name: Hongdae Night
stops.description: Seoul's best nightlife strip. Craft beer bars, rooftop cocktail lounges, and clubs that run until morning. Every music genre, every vibe.
stops.tip: Thursday Party is the classic backpacker bar crawl starting point. Club FF for electronic. Always check cover charges upfront.

title: Jamsil High & Low
fitReason: The world's 5th tallest building, Seoul's famous theme park, and cherry blossom lakeside walks — all in one district.

stops.name: Seokchon Lake Morning Walk
stops.description: A peaceful lakeside loop around the lake beside Lotte World. Cherry blossoms in spring, firefly lights in winter — always beautiful.
stops.tip: The full loop is 2.5 km and takes about 30 minutes. Best before 10 AM when it's quiet. Lotte World Tower reflects perfectly in the lake.

stops.name: Lotte World Mall
stops.description: One of Korea's largest entertainment malls — luxury brands, aquarium, cinema, and the full K-culture experience under one massive roof.
stops.tip: The aquarium is world-class and kid-friendly. Top floor food court has good views of Seokchon Lake.

stops.name: Lotte World Mall Food Hall
stops.description: Multiple food floors with Korean, Japanese, and international options. The mid-tower food court has the best view while you eat.
stops.tip: Go to the upper floors for Korean BBQ sets. The basement has convenience store-level prices for quick bites.

stops.name: Seoul Sky Observatory
stops.description: 555 meters up in the 5th tallest building in the world — the glass floor section is terrifying in the best way. Views stretch to Incheon on clear days.
stops.tip: Book tickets online to skip the queue. Sunset visits (5–7 PM) are the most popular — book 2 days ahead for weekends.

stops.name: Olympic Park
stops.description: The 1988 Seoul Olympics site is now a sprawling park full of outdoor sculptures, cycling paths, and weekend concert stages. One of Seoul's best-kept secrets.
stops.tip: The Rose Garden peaks in May. The outdoor concert lawn (Mongchontoseong) has free performances on summer weekends.

stops.name: Jamsil Dinner
stops.description: The streets around Lotte World have excellent Korean BBQ, grilled pork belly spots, and late-night pojangmacha tents.
stops.tip: Samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) restaurants fill up fast after 7 PM — walk in early or wait. Soju is mandatory.

title: Myeongdong to Namsan
fitReason: K-beauty shopping, one of Seoul's most iconic towers, and a traditional village all within walking distance.

stops.name: Namsangol Hanok Village
stops.description: Five restored traditional hanok houses at the foot of Namsan mountain. Free entry, weekend cultural performances, and a time capsule buried for the year 2394.
stops.tip: Free entry. The traditional courtyard in the back has the best photo spots. Performances on weekend afternoons.

stops.transit: Cable car or bus 15 min up Namsan

stops.name: N Seoul Tower
stops.description: Seoul's most recognizable landmark at the summit of Namsan. The love lock fence has millions of locks. The 360° night view is why people come back.
stops.tip: Combination ticket (cable car + observation deck) saves money. Go up at sunset for the best views.

stops.transit: Cable car or walk 30 min down to Myeongdong

stops.name: Myeongdong Kyoja
stops.description: Seoul's most famous noodle restaurant since 1966. Hand-cut kalguksu in a dense chicken broth, and dumplings so good they have their own Michelin recognition.
stops.tip: Order the kalguksu and a side of the mandu (dumplings). Lines go around the block at 12 PM — arrive at 1:30 PM to skip the worst of it.

stops.name: Myeongdong K-Beauty District
stops.description: The highest concentration of K-beauty flagships in the world — Innisfree, Etude, Laneige, Sulwhasoo, and Olive Young all within a few blocks.
stops.tip: Staff in every store push free samples aggressively — use this to test before you buy. Prices are similar everywhere so shop by preference.

stops.name: Namdaemun Market
stops.description: Korea's largest traditional market, operating since 1414. Wholesale clothes, Korean kitchenware, dried goods, and the best hotteok (sweet pancake) in Seoul.
stops.tip: The hotteok vendor near the main entrance (Gate 5) always has a line — completely worth it. Bring small bills for street food vendors.

stops.name: Myeongdong Dinner
stops.description: The side streets off main Myeongdong-gil have excellent Korean restaurants — dak galbi, samgyeopsal, bibimbap sets in the ₩10,000–₩15,000 range.
stops.tip: Avoid the restaurants with plastic food displays and photo menus — walk one block off the tourist strip for real prices.

title: Itaewon & Beyond
fitReason: World-class art, Seoul's most international food scene, and cocktail bars that rival anywhere in the world.

stops.name: Leeum Samsung Museum of Art
stops.description: One of Asia's finest private museums — ancient Korean celadon ceramics alongside Damien Hirst and Nam June Paik. The building itself (by Rem Koolhaas) is a work of art.
stops.tip: Free on the first Sunday of each month. Audio guide is worth the ₩2,000. The gift shop has beautiful Korean ceramics reproductions.

stops.name: Itaewon Antique Furniture Street
stops.description: A street of antique dealers selling Korean furniture, Joseon-era ceramics, and vintage objects. Serious collectors and casual browsers welcome.
stops.tip: Prices are negotiable. Ask the shop owners about provenance — most speak some English and love talking about their pieces.

stops.name: Itaewon International Lunch
stops.description: Seoul's most diverse food block — Japanese ramen, Indian curry, Middle Eastern mezze, and Italian all on the same street. Best area in Seoul for non-Korean food.
stops.tip: The alleys behind the main Itaewon road (Haebangchon direction) have better prices and less tourist traffic.

stops.name: Haebangchon (HBC) Café Crawl
stops.description: The charming hillside neighborhood above Itaewon with indie cafés, local bars, and a neighborhood feel you won't find in more tourist-heavy areas.
stops.tip: Walk up the hill to Gyeongrinan-gil — the views back toward Namsan are great. Most cafés here are quiet enough to actually work or read.

stops.name: Itaewon Vintage Shops
stops.description: The best vintage and secondhand clothing in Seoul — the main street and its side alleys have dozens of curated shops.
stops.tip: Prices on the main drag are tourist-adjusted. The shops down the hill toward Noksapyeong are cheaper and better curated.

stops.name: Itaewon Craft Cocktail Bars
stops.description: The cocktail bar alley off the main Itaewon strip has some of the best craft drinks in Asia. Creative Korean-inspired cocktails at surprisingly reasonable prices.
stops.tip: Charles H at Four Seasons is worth the splurge for one round. For more casual, Bar Cham and Southside Parlor are excellent.
